title: Device and Runtime Heterogeneity Dominate Delivered Latency: Benchmarking Mobile Vision Transformers for Fine-Grained Classification on Commodity Smartphones
content: Latency measured on a single reference handset is usually not a reliable basis for deployment decisions. Field devices differ in hardware and runtime backend, so architectures that appear efficient in published benchmarks may be recommended incorrectly for the devices that actually run them. This work aims to bridge this gap. Three mobile architectures–MobileNetV2-100, MobileViT-XXS, and EfficientFormerV2-S0–are benchmarked on 2,721 medicinal plant species (303,165 images) under four preprocessing variants and three seeds, against a ViT-Base/16 ceiling trained on identical partitions, and six deployed LiteRT artifacts are measured on three commodity Android handsets. The findings suggest that latency characterizes the device–model–runtime triple rather than the network alone: identical artifacts span 188 ms to 5341 ms, the fastest architecture on one handset is slowest on another, and the deployment recommendation reverses when a second device enters the benchmark. Half-precision conversion halves artifact size without reducing latency. The findings further suggest that EfficientFormerV2-S0 recovers 81.4% of the ceiling with 4.9% of its parameters, whereas MobileViT-XXS trails MobileNetV2-100 because its classifier head consumes 47.9% of its parameters. Engineered preprocessing reduces accuracy in all 45 paired comparisons. These results support multi-device benchmarking as a practical prerequisite for deploying offline intelligent classifiers in the field.
